author: WP20
summary: A process chapter for porting XNA/FNA games: freeze a baseline, translate mechanically, map assets and shaders to concrete routes, choose renderers by evidence, make services and timing explicit, verify in rungs and troubleshoot by boundary. Several content and renderer facts were stale (CNA writes XNB/CNB, LZ4 is decoded, 14 compiled-effect identities, five model routes, run-time renderer selection). The site had the API-level migration guide and tutorials but not the process; it now lives on a new practice deep dive with the workflow figure recreated.

concepts.section: Migrating an XNA or FNA Game to CNA
concepts.text: CNA keeps much of XNA's public shape in C++ but does not make a C# game binary- or source-compatible; a migration is a controlled translation with explicit asset, renderer, service and verification decisions.

target.evidence: CHECKLIST.md; modules/*/include (C++ headers mirror XNA namespaces)

concepts.section: Freeze a behavioral baseline first
concepts.text: Before porting, pin the original at a named commit and capture deterministic simulation traces, screenshots, saves, network packets, audio events and an asset inventory, together with resolution, fixed-step interval, random seeds, locale and platform.

target.evidence: methodology; CNA reference tools named on the page: tools/xna-oracle (39 scenes)

concepts.section: Freeze a behavioral baseline first
concepts.text: Classify the starting point: a C# XNA/FNA game needs a language translation, while an existing C++ reconstruction needs only its platform-service boundary replaced; the two risks must be kept separate.

target.evidence: methodology; illustrated by mobile-eggbert @d43c6a1 (translation) and the free-eggbert cna.md study (boundary replacement)

concepts.section: Freeze a behavioral baseline first
concepts.text: Translating game logic and redesigning rendering in one pass destroys the ability to attribute a mismatch; change one layer at a time and compare after each.
tokens: destroys the ability to attribute a mismatch

concepts.section: Translate the API shape mechanically
concepts.text: Namespaces map from dots to C++ scopes; C# property reads and writes become getValueProperty()/setValueProperty(value); events, nullables, collections, ownership and ref/out need explicit C++ idioms.

target.evidence: CHECKLIST.md; SharpRuntime DEF_PROP/IMPL_PROP accessor pairs, e.g. modules/graphics/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/Viewport.hpp

concepts.section: Translate the API shape mechanically
concepts.text: Do not redesign names while translating: reach compiling, comparable code first; compiler errors are an inventory while the translation is mechanical, and broad wrapper layers can make an unimplemented CNA behaviour look like a game bug.
tokens: Do not redesign names while translating

concepts.section: Translate the API shape mechanically
concepts.text: Compiling the translated game with CNA_STRICT_XNA_API turns every CNAEXT marker into [[deprecated]], so the build lists every place the port relies on a CNA extension rather than on XNA API.
concepts.note: Extends the figure's 'strict-XNA compile' step with the TARGET mechanism.

concepts.section: Inventory content by actual reader route
concepts.text: CNA reads real XNB files (container, LZX, a registered reader table, shared resources, stock effects, graphics, models, audio); statements that XNB is unsupported are false.
concepts.note: The Bible's fixture count (30) is not carried; TARGET has 181 .xnb files in the tree and the site does not publish a fixture count.

concepts.section: Inventory content by actual reader route
concepts.text: Claim that CNA does not produce XNB files: at TARGET the build-time cna-content tool writes both XNB and CNB.
tokens: writes both XNB and CNA's own CNB container
concepts.note: Corrected on the page: CNA now writes XNB and CNB at build time.

concepts.section: Inventory content by actual reader route
concepts.text: The XNB reader registry is explicit, not reflective: custom types need ContentTypeReaderManager::AddTypeCreator or a declared field list through ReflectiveTypeReaderBuilder.
concepts.note: Corrected: a declared-field reflective builder exists at TARGET; only automatic discovery is absent.

concepts.section: Inventory content by actual reader route
concepts.text: Claim that LZ4-compressed XNB is refused: at TARGET the typed load path decodes one raw LZ4 block (flag 0x40) with CNA's own decoder.
concepts.note: Corrected: LZ4 is decoded on the typed Load<T> path; the untyped external-reference decoder still refuses it (content-robustness page).

concepts.section: Inventory content by actual reader route
concepts.text: The general EffectReader reads a bounded bytecode blob and constructs Effect(GraphicsDevice&, bytes), which accepts D3D9 Effect Framework binaries only where the renderer has compiled effects; the five stock-effect XNB readers are a separate route.

concepts.section: Inventory content by actual reader route
concepts.text: Loose assets use CNJ descriptors, native image/audio/video formats or direct glTF/GLB loading; runtime glTF and offline gltf_to_cnj share one import core but keep route-specific limits.

target.evidence: modules/content/src/Xna/ContentManager.cpp (loose readers); glTF import core per deep-dives/models/gltf-import.html

concepts.section: Inventory content by actual reader route
concepts.text: A migration manifest maps every source asset to its route, reader, sidecars and verification oracle, and every asset is tested against the selected route instead of being judged by its extension (the load ladder lets a stale sibling win).

concepts.section: Treat custom shaders as renderer contracts
concepts.text: Claim that compiled effects run on FNA3D and behind opt-in switches on SDL_GPU, EasyGL and Vulkan only: at TARGET 14 of 25 identities in 10 families (FNA3D always; nine default-off options incl. WebGPU, Software, DirectX 9/11/12, OpenGL 4).
tokens: 14 of the 25 renderer identities in 10 families
concepts.note: Corrected to the canonical 14/25 identities, 10 families.

concepts.section: Treat custom shaders as renderer contracts
concepts.text: Inventory the exact shader byte format: HLSL .fx source, DXBC and MonoGame MGFX are different inputs that CNA does not accept at run time; build-time .fx compilation goes through an external legacy compiler.

target.evidence: docs/fx-compiled-effects.md; site canonical facts (cna-content external fxc)

concepts.section: Treat custom shaders as renderer contracts
concepts.text: ShaderEffect is the separate source/program route whose accepted language depends on the renderer, so the target renderer set must be chosen before the shader strategy; portable games may need per-family programs or stock effects.
tokens: choose the target renderer set first, then the shader strategy

concepts.section: Audit vertex layouts and model assumptions
concepts.text: The glTF importer packs into a small closed set of strides that the upload path treats as an ABI; a custom VertexDeclaration is only guaranteed on the direct-buffer route.
concepts.note: Bible's 'seven strides / eight upload cases' detail is on the vertex-packing page.

concepts.section: Audit vertex layouts and model assumptions
concepts.text: For each vertex format record element offsets, formats, usages, stride, index width, primitive topology and the data's source route.
tokens: element offsets, formats, usages, stride, index width, primitive topology

concepts.section: Audit vertex layouts and model assumptions
concepts.text: Claim that models have four routes: at TARGET five content routes (XNB, CNB, self-contained CNJ, direct glTF/GLB, legacy skinned manifest) plus hand-built objects; skinning keeps separate joint, scene-node and palette index spaces.
concepts.note: Corrected from four to five routes.

concepts.section: Select a renderer by evidence, not by name
concepts.text: A build chooses from 25 public identities over 21 families at configure time (CNA_GRAPHICS_RENDERER), or compiles a list for run-time choice (CNA_GRAPHICS_RENDERERS); filter by admissibility, then capability, then evidence tier.
tokens: 25 public renderer identities over 21 implementation families
concepts.note: Corrected: selection is not only a single CMake-time value; multi-renderer builds select at run time.

target.evidence: cmake/RendererSelection.cmake (CNA_GRAPHICS_RENDERERS, TERMINAL and Emscripten refusals); cmake/RendererIdentities.cmake

concepts.section: Select a renderer by evidence, not by name
concepts.text: Configure-time admissibility examples: OPENGLES3 is refused under Emscripten (WEBGL2 is its spelling there), Direct3D identities build only for Windows targets, and the TERMINAL platform accepts only SOFTWARE, PORTABLEGL, HEADLESS and STUB.

concepts.section: Select a renderer by evidence, not by name
concepts.text: Start on one well-verified desktop renderer, add a structurally independent control, then cross to web or mobile; compile the same game for each identity, avoid renderer conditionals, and never count a coloured fallback or headless skip as parity.

concepts.section: Make service differences explicit
concepts.text: Service implementations are not equally deep: GamerServices has synthetic local identities and local JSON persistence, Local network sessions deliver nothing, web saves live in memory unless the page adds persistence, and video depends on the optional FFmpeg backend.
tokens: a Local session delivers no packets
concepts.note: Storage selector/file containment and Android lifecycle coverage are left to their own pages (docs/storage.html, android-and-apple-platforms).

target.evidence: modules/net/src/Xna/NetworkSession.cpp; modules/gamer-services; site deep dives (network-sessions, gamer-services-contract, web-build-and-main-loop)

concepts.section: Make service differences explicit
concepts.text: Set TargetElapsedTime from the original simulation (CNA defaults to 166,667 ticks and a fixed step; the setter rejects non-positive spans) and decide pause, inactive sleep, slow frames, variable step and shutdown per host; the browser loop differs from native.

concepts.section: Build a verification ladder for the port
concepts.text: A verification ladder uses increasingly independent checks: compile-time surface, renderer-free logic tests, asset-load tests with malformed input, small golden checks, differential comparison with the frozen original, a second renderer, and host engagement evidence.
tokens: Deterministic logic tests with no renderer
A second renderer as a localisation control

target.evidence: methodology; instruments named on the page exist at TARGET (HEADLESS/STUB renderers, tools/xna-oracle)

concepts.section: Build a verification ladder for the port
concepts.text: Record skips and runtime identity: Wine results must prove translator engagement, browser results need an out-of-process frame verdict, mobile results keep package, logs, screenshot and lifecycle trace; built everywhere is not behaves everywhere.

concepts.section: Troubleshoot from the boundary inward
concepts.text: Configure failures usually mean a name outside the 25 identities, a missing sibling (sharp-runtime next), an inadmissible platform/renderer pair or a source-changing option; keep the configure command and the generated CNA_RENDERER_<ID> / CNA_MULTI_RENDERER definitions; link failures expose module ownership or missing runtime libraries.
tokens: a renderer name outside the 25 public identities

concepts.section: Troubleshoot from the boundary inward
concepts.text: Classify the first runtime failure (asset resolution, reader registration, window/device creation, frame lifetime, renderer engagement, behavioural oracle), keep the original exception and the smallest reproducer; the goal is that every red result names the boundary that failed.
tokens: every red result names the boundary that failed
